historical_reviews.deepseek: Provides no SWC-specific register/status or measured rail outcome.

original_test_intent: Exercise the DDR5 PMIC SWC fatal fault on each applicable DIMM and voltage comparator, confirm the intended reset and a fresh SWC/railtype2-specific report, and verify the SWC rail, memory channel and management interface recover.
original_method: Obtain the PMIC register map that binds SWC to railtype2 and voltage types; build a per-DIMM socket/die/UMC/slot/PMIC-address matrix; identify BMC/platform I2C ownership; record SWC telemetry/status baseline; inject one tuple under OOB observation; correlate exact rail status and persistent error; validate reset, training and memory; restore PMIC/I2C configuration before a separately approved next tuple.
manual_activity: The PMIC/BIOS owner supplies the SWC register/rail map, approves each DIMM and voltage comparator, supervises one fatal run at a time and restores rail, I2C and memory state.
required_inputs: PMIC datasheet/register proof that railtype2 selects SWC and definitions of voltagetype0/1
Per-DIMM socket/die/UMC/channel/slot/dimm and PMIC part/address topology
Wistron BMC/platform I2C controller, bus, address, OOB path and expected SWC register response
Vendor-correct command continuation and full tuple-expansion matrix
SWC rail nominal/range, monitored status bits, current/temperature limits and hard aborts
Fresh railtype2 PMIC/CPER/BERT/SEL evidence, reset/boot/training timeouts, memory recovery and rollback
safety_requirements: Dedicated DDR5 SUT with independent console and rail telemetry suitable for SWC
Verify PMIC part revision and map telemetry/status to the selected physical DIMM
Execute one voltage comparator on one DIMM once; restore and validate before another
Abort on wrong rail/status bit, unsafe voltage/current/temperature, unexpected reset, training timeout, DIMM loss, I2C failure or ambiguous evidence
No automatic traversal; restore SPD ownership, telemetry polling, I2C enables, PMIC mode/recovery and HDT state
agent_execution_scope: Validate SWC/railtype2 register semantics, target matrix, I2C ownership, telemetry envelope and recovery
Collect read-only raw PMIC/I2C settings, rail status, OOB/CPER/BERT/SEL, DIMM training and memory health
Do not infer rail/comparator/target, alter PMIC/I2C/BIOS/HDT, inject, reset, repeat, recover or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Approve SWC rail/register and per-target matrix
Approve telemetry limits and rail-specific fatal oracle
Restore PMIC/I2C/memory state and issue verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Shared PMIC log keywords cannot prove railtype2 selected SWC, identify voltage comparator or distinguish the target from SWA/SWB/SWD.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the PMIC register map and physical DIMM topology to run one railtype2 tuple, correlate the exact SWC status/telemetry and persistent record, then verify training and memory before any next target.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: listvalidumc, socketdieumc0:0:3, railtype2, voltagetype0/1, dimm0, immediate reset, all-DIMM scope, PMIC/I2C settings and 360/120-minute values remain preserved but gated.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Run a register-backed SWC matrix serially, one physical PMIC/comparator at a time, with rail-specific telemetry and complete recovery evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds SWC register identity, cross-rail discrimination, PMIC address/I2C ownership, tuple expansion, electrical aborts and restoration proof.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Reset and generic PMIC logs cannot prove SWC coverage, and a fixed dimm0 tuple cannot cover the requested population.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Selecting the wrong rail or comparator can disrupt a different memory power domain and invalidate both coverage and recovery.

project_override_considerations: The I2C path is platform-management scope under the Wistron rule. Require the controller/bus/address and vendor response; do not accept a host Linux bus listing. Keep SWC evidence separate from other rail-type cases even when reset behavior looks identical.
expected_evidence: SWC register/railtype2/voltagetype mapping and complete physical DIMM/PMIC/I2C matrix
Pinned tool/spec and raw SWC telemetry/status plus BIOS/SPD baseline
Exact per-target command and OOB reset/boot timeline
Fresh SWC-specific PMIC status and CPER/BERT/SEL source/severity fields
In-range restored SWC rail, full DIMM training/enumeration and clean bounded memory workload
Restoration diff and engineer verdict per tuple

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: All DIMMs and two voltage types are required, but only 0:0:3/dimm0/voltagetype0 is specified and no mapping rule exists. The split command is syntactically ambiguous. Railtype2-to-SWC, comparator meanings and I2C ownership are not proven, and acceptance lacks rail-specific electrical criteria.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The SWC fatal-rail purpose and seed command are explicit. Required vendor mapping and electrical limits can be supplied as execution prerequisites, so static review completes.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 90 Wistron-System RAS-00810-V002: provide PMIC register proof railtype2=SWC and voltagetype0/1 meanings; map every DIMM to socket/die/UMC/channel/slot/dimm, PMIC part/address and Wistron BMC/platform I2C controller/bus/OOB path; approve command continuation and full tuple matrix; define SWC-specific status/telemetry limits, PMIC/CPER/BERT/SEL evidence, reset/boot/training deadlines, memory recovery, aborts and complete restoration.

review_improvement: Makes SWC distinguishable from adjacent rails through register and telemetry evidence and replaces the fixed tuple with a traceable per-DIMM comparator matrix.
independent_technical_reasoning: PMIC rail faults can have identical high-level reset symptoms, so railtype2 must be verified against a SWC-specific status bit and telemetry channel. The two voltage-type values likely select different comparisons, but their meaning cannot be inferred. Coverage therefore depends on physical PMIC addressing and a per-DIMM tuple, followed by rail restoration and memory-training checks; generic dmesg cannot supply that proof.
